sources.claim: Illinois HB 3773 amended the Illinois Human Rights Act, effective January 1, 2026: employers may not use AI in a way that discriminates against protected classes, may not use ZIP codes as a proxy for protected classes, and must give notice when AI is used for covered employment decisions.

sections.skill: Recognize a proxy for a protected trait

questions.prompt: What is a proxy in this context?

choices.text: A person who votes for someone else in an election when they cannot attend in person
An input that stands in for something else

questions.correct_answer: An input that stands in for something else
questions.intro: A PROXY is an input that stands in for something else. In fairness, the concern is a proxy for a PROTECTED TRAIT, such as race, sex, age or disability, that anti-discrimination rules protect. Removing the trait itself does not prevent bias if a proxy remains. ZIP code can stand in for race in places where neighborhoods are segregated; a gap in employment history can stand in for caregiving and therefore sex. One example in law: Illinois amended its Human Rights Act, effective January 1, 2026, so employers may not use ZIP codes as a proxy for protected classes in AI-assisted employment decisions.

sections.skill: Compare a proxy with guessing someone's age from their music

questions.prompt: In the example, what is the proxy?

choices.text: Age, which is the trait that was written on the form in the very first place

questions.intro: If you removed "age" from a form but kept "favorite radio station," you might still guess age pretty well: some stations mostly attract older listeners, others younger. The radio station is a PROXY for age. A model can do the same thing: even without the protected trait, it may find inputs that point to it and repeat unfair patterns.

questions.prompt: What trait does the proxy point to?

choices.text: Height, since people who listen to the radio are usually taller than average

questions.prompt: Shopping habits, first names and commute times together reveal a protected trait. What does this show?

choices.text: That each input is a proxy on its own, so each one must always be removed separately

questions.intro: Proxies are not always obvious. A combination of harmless-looking inputs, such as shopping habits, first names and commute times, can together reveal a protected trait. Some proxies also carry real information for the task, which makes the choice harder. Teams should test outcomes across groups even when protected traits are not used as inputs, and be ready to explain why each input is needed.

questions.prompt: An input carries real task information and is also a proxy. What makes this hard?
